 Order

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved with award dated 30.07.2005 passed by the XIth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur in MVC No.98/02 by which the appellant has been directed to pay the compensation to the respondent/claimant and the Insurance Company has been exonerated from the liability to compensate the claimant and insured.

entities.text: XIth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts giving rise to this appeal are that on 18.05.2002 at 23:30 the claimants were travelling on the Tractor of deceased Ramphal Patel who was the owner and the driver of the vehicle and by rash and negligent driving, he turned the Tractor as a result the passenger sitting on the vehicle got injury and two persons died on the spot and the victims were sent to Victoria Hospital, Jabalpur.
FIR was lodged at the Police Station- Majgawan.
Police registered the case and on that basis the claim petition was filed.

3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of vehicle owner's/deceased Ramphal Patel's wife has submitted that as per Ex.P-1, the FIR was lodged against the MP-20-HA-0130 and the police on the next day after incident seized the Vehicle No.MP-20-HA-0136 and that vehicle was mechanically Smt.Radha Bai vs Maniram Kol on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154942891/
1 examined but the claim petition has been filed against the driver/owner of the vehicle No.MP-20-HA-0137 and the Claim Tribunal has wrongly allowed the claim petition and has not considered the above facts.
He further submitted that the Insurance Company has wrongly been exonerated.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 has supported the award passed by the Claim Tribunal and prayed to dismiss this appeal.
5. I have heard the parties and gone through the record.
6. In this case the appellant has based the claim on the basis of FIR (Ex.P-1) for that reason the FIR is more important document in this case.

The FIR was lodged by Madan Gotiya and in that it is written that on the date of incident 18.05.2002 they were going in the Barat of his son Sohanlal on the Tractor No.MP-20-HA-0130 which was driven by Ramphal Patel resident of Chandu Deori and in the trolly of the tractor, 30 to 40 persons were travelling.
Barat was going from Pratappur to Silondi.

Ramphal Patel was driving the tractor rashly and negligently and the person travelling on the tractor objected, when they reached near Postmortem House, the tractor's Trolly turned and all the persons travelling in the trolly suffered injuries and Om Prakas and Mukesh Gotiya died on the spot.
Thus, in the FIR it was stated that the tractor was being driven by Ramphal Patel son of Chandu Patel resident of Chandu Deori.

7. As per the document submitted by the claimants and as per Ex.P-2, on 19.05.2002 at 10:40 am from the spot near Postmortem House Majhgawan, the Tractor No. MP-20-HA-0136 whose engine number and chassis number clearly mentioned was recovered and seized and along with tractor the registration certificate of the vehicle MP-20-HA-0136 was also recovered and in that the name of vehicle owner was Ramphal Patel son of Ramdas Patel resident of Chandu Deori.
As per mechanical report (Ex.P-3), the vehicle No. MP-20-HA- 0136 was examined and as per that the vehicle owner was Ramphal Patel resident of Chandu Deori.
8. Maniram (PW-1) in his statement has clearly stated that the offending vehicle was of the ownership of Ramphal and he himself was driving the vehicle.
Prakash Gondane (NAW-2) has stated that the tractor MP-20-HA-0136 was insured with the Insurance Company and he has further stated that as per Policy Ramphal was the owner of the vehicle.

Radha Bai herself has admitted that her husband's tractor number is MP-20-HA-0136.
9.

Looking from this aspect, it is clear that from very beginning, clear cut FIR was lodged against Ramphal Patel resident of Village Chandu Deori and if mathematics number in Devnagri Script and in English number, 137 and 136 have wrongly mentioned, it does not affect the case as the name of vehicle owner and driver have been clearly mentioned.

It is admitted that the vehicle No.MP-20-HA-0136 belongs to deceased respondent Ramphal Patel husband of the appellant Radha Bai, so on this technical aspect the well reasoned claim cannot be rejected.

It is clear from the FIR itself that on the date of incident on that vehicle the passengers were carried out and it has not been proved that the owner has taken special permission to carry the Barat, hence, the vehicle was clearly being operated against the Insurance Policy, hence, Insurance Company is not liable to Smt.Radha Bai vs Maniram Kol on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154942891/
2
compensate the insured.
10. Hence, this miscellaneous appeal sans merit and is hereby dismissed.
11. With the copy of this order, record of the Claims Tribunal be returned back.
12. Record of the appeal be consigned to record room.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE DPS Smt.Radha Bai vs Maniram Kol on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154942891/
